defect_reproduction.source_cause: A committed paper fill was published as five separately-admitted lifecycle events (risk_evaluation, order_submitted, order_accepted, fill, position_snapshot). Any build/persistence failure (or interruption) after the first admission leaves a partial chain; before this fix an exception from the sink propagated out of execute() into SignalConsumer, which would DLQ the signal and leave its fence in_progress. Saved evidence for the original signal shows only an execution_in_progress_elsewhere noop (original signal DLQ readonly proof contains no unexpected_error entry); the kernel stop was SOURCE-INGEST, not the paper runtime.
defect_reproduction.caveat: UNKNOWN / 無法確認: the original close-interruption trigger/exception and original broker metadata are not established by retained logs (operator-accepted explicit unknown). Injected failures are regression scenarios only; the earlier 'inferred from outbox' trigger statement is not proof.

paper_runtime.py: Committed-fill lifecycle chain (risk, order_submitted, order_accepted, fill, position_snapshot) is staged and admitted in ONE atomic outbox write (LifecycleTelemetryOutbox.admit_many) with an idempotency batch id; no partial chain is possible.

Each committed fill is staged in the existing per-binding paper performance ledger (pending_fill_publications, written before the sink runs, same precedent as pending_performance_pair) and acknowledged only after durable admission.

PaperRuntimeService._on_order_event no longer lets a publication failure escape after the ledger committed (no DLQ, fence completes, no second trade); the staged fill is replayed on the next drain/restart with the original identities (event_id, broker_order_id, trade_episode_id, envelope) and deterministic payloads (position values come from the committed fill, created_at from the fill).

_admit_lifecycle_batch adopts the durable outbox chain (not the re-staged in-memory chain) after admission, so replaying an already-admitted batch (ack failed, same process or restart) no longer leaves memory sequence ahead of disk; the next non-trading event is contiguous (previously memory seq 12 vs disk 7 then 'admission sequence is not contiguous').

Outbox admitted_batches is no longer truncated by count (was [-512:]); a batch id is released (LifecycleTelemetryOutbox.release_batch) only after the ledger acknowledges the fill publication, so a replay after >512 intervening batches (same process or restart) still hits the idempotent no-op and keeps the original sequence_no (regression: test_replay_after_many_batches_same_process/restart).
runtime_summary.py: pnl/drawdown snapshots carry the authoritative ledger fill_count; when it exceeds the fill events projected, fill-derived positions are withheld (positions=[], position_count=null, positions_status=unavailable, reason fill_event_gap) instead of presenting a stale open position. Missing pnl/drawdown/sharpe stay absent, never zero.

Heartbeat performance_telemetry.fill_count (existing genuine field, present even for status=unchanged) also feeds ledger_fill_count, so an upgraded projector with a stored fill1/short1 summary and an unchanged flat ledger (pending_performance_pair null, no new pnl/drawdown snapshot) withholds the stale short 1 without any new quote/trade/fill or event time.
unchanged: signal idempotency and execution fence semantics (signal_consumer.py untouched)
